P1.evidence: The best setter-notes handling in the batch alongside the Craig call: 'I already got some information from Derek, but I would just like to go through where you're at at the moment, where you want to go, hear everything from you' — and he used those notes later ('I heard from Derek and that's of course with the cutting down'). The frame carried two of four parts with the disqualification promise, and agreement was sought and given. The open question survives only as a stub — 'So tell me' — after which the prospect delivered four unbroken minutes of self-briefing, which set the pattern for the whole call.

P2.evidence: Nutrition was properly covered and produced the most useful material on the call — the fructose intolerance, the wife's cooking as the point of failure, the meal-variety problem, the calorie-tracking history. Current training was established clearly. Everything else was skipped or arrived by luck. Weight came from the prospect; age and height were never asked. Occupation was never asked, which is the striking one: 'I just finished medical residency' and 'I am in the Air Force' were both volunteered inside the first four minutes and neither was pursued for a single follow-up, despite being the two most ICP-relevant facts anyone said on this call. Health conditions were never asked, and the prospect volunteered 'I had gotten sick previously. That was pretty long-standing sickness' — no follow-up at all. Injuries were never asked; only mobility, via a 1-to-10 scale. Sleep and energy were never asked in a thirty-minute call with a doctor coming off residency.

P3.evidence: Two checks ran and neither was built on. The mobility question was good and included a why — 'why do you feel like you do want to make that better because, of course, the average American is okay with it and it sounds like you're not' — which produced a genuinely useful answer about avoiding the bodybuilder trap. The bridge also ran: 'when it comes to getting more confident, what did you mean with that?' That produced the single best line of the call — 'with working out, just being disciplined is keeping promises to yourself... I found that when I was working out with the coach, I was probably the most confident I've ever been' — and the rep responded with a one-word reflection and moved to the next topic. No future-self question, no who-else-does-this-impact despite a wife being mentioned five times, and nothing driven toward identity, marriage or longevity. The closing summary was a needs list ('accountability, the structure, a plan in place, those three things'), not a reframe. The phase was reachable, the material was offered up freely, and it was left on the floor.

P4.evidence: The one phase run properly. The full attempt history came out — the coach three years ago, 185 to 155 in sixteen weeks, the prescribed bulk, the smaller cuts, the tracking apps — and what happened to each was traced, including the two specific failure points: 'just kind of fell off once I started residency' and 'as soon as my wife came into play... I just fell off because she'd make better food'. The root-cause question was asked properly and with a forward edge: 'do you think that that was just a temporary thing, or is that something that would still be going on at the moment, because we would coach you for six months, but we don't want you to just fall off again after that, so how are you going to make sure that you're actually going to stick to it?' That produced the gap in the prospect's own words: 'I think it's decision fatigue... being able to just have a plan and someone tell me to do something is easier.' P4f is partial because the prospect said the information-is-not-the-problem line himself and the rep only reflected it back.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form. No two-year question, no settle question, no why-not, no line in the sand. The absence is more costly here than on most calls in this batch, because the prospect's own objection is a timing objection — he wants to start in six weeks — and Phase 5 is the phase that makes waiting expensive. He had also handed over the raw material: a year without training, a physique he has already lost once, and a self-described pattern of not starting when he cannot do it perfectly.

P6.evidence: Not attempted at any point. No belief question, no going-all-in question, no yes of any kind was sought before or after the pricing discussion. The nearest thing is the timing probe at 00:20:19 — 'let's say you would see that with us, and you feel like, yeah, this actually is exactly what I'm looking for... Would you then still be like, no, we're gonna wait a month?' — which tests the deferral rather than the commitment, and drew 'Probably, to be honest'. The call ran as a product Q&A from beginning to end and never converted into a sale process.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted, so the phase drops out of the denominator. No price was ever stated, no offer was formally presented, and the rep proposed reconvening rather than proceeding: 'if you feel like this is something that you're interested in, but maybe the investment is a bit on the higher end at the moment in your thoughts, we can just jump on like right before or right after that test.'

objection_plays.detail: The central objection on the call and the only one the rep engaged. The premise was tested once and well — 'Would you then still be like, no, we're gonna wait a month?' — but on 'Probably, to be honest' the rep immediately conceded and proposed booking a month out. None of the scripted moves ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now', and crucially no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled', which is the move that answers this exact objection. The prospect's stated reason is that he wants to do only push-ups, sit-ups and running for six weeks — a claim that a coach-built programme could plausibly have accommodated, and nobody proposed it.

'That would be more than what I'd want to spend' is a clear money trigger from a newly-qualified physician who had already told the rep that price would decide it — 'if the price isn't right, then I'm just not going to be wanting to go with you guys'. Not one move ran. No isolation, no should-I-versus-how frame, no upfront-or-plan option, and none of the six financial-picture questions. The rep instead answered an unrelated question about how Trevor selects clients. This is the most complete OC miss in the batch, against the prospect in the batch most obviously able to pay.

Script gap: a technically literate buyer running a structured vendor evaluation. He said so outright — 'I've seen multiple different kettlebell teams trying to do this' and 'I'd rather set up meetings and talk to you guys over the next couple of weeks and find the person that works for me' — and then ran a product interrogation: how do you cover all body groups without pulling movements, how does progressive overload work with kettlebells, which app, what is the check-in cadence, how is form reviewed, how many sessions, which diet. There is no play for this and no product sheet to answer it from, and the rep never converted the evaluation into a sale process. The prospect's central technical question, about back and pulling work, was raised twice and never answered — even though it is what attracted him to Primal in the first place.

Second gap: the rep attempted to extract the prospect's budget before naming a price — 'what is sort of the range in which you're looking to invest in your own personal growth?' — and the prospect refused and reversed it: 'I'd rather have you guys recommend the price because you guys are familiar with what your costs are... if you guys share with me a price, I'll tell you if that's where I can.' There is no scripted handling for a prospect who declines to anchor first, and what followed was three successive non-answers and eventually a $2,000-to-$8,000 range.

notes: The strongest ICP fit in the batch — a physician finishing residency, in the Air Force, restarting after a year out — and the weakest sales process run against anyone. Phase 4 was genuinely good and everything after it was absent: no consequence frame, no commitment check, no money play, and no price. Two specific coaching points. First, the prospect handed over depth material unprompted at 00:12:00 ('keeping promises to yourself... I was probably the most confident I've ever been') and it was acknowledged in one word and dropped; that is the call. Second, when a prospect asks the price directly three times, answer it — the escalating non-answers ended in a $2,000-to-$8,000 range that a comparison shopper will read as either a discount signal or a red flag, and either way it is not the offer. Escalate the pricing language itself rather than coaching it; it is not a slip, it is a different offer.
